title: Implement tiered batching selection in runtime config schema (batching_tier) with validation + precedence
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Goal
Add a tier selector to the runtime config schema so customers (and internal config surfaces) can choose recommended batching defaults: fast / standard / cost_efficient.

This ticket is schema + validation + precedence only. Runtime mapping logic (tier -> concrete scheduler params) is tracked separately.

Background
We’re shipping workload-aware batching defaults. To ship safely across Hosted/Dedicated/Private we need an explicit, versioned config knob with clear precedence vs existing explicit batching settings.

Proposed schema change
- Add optional field: batching_tier
  - Enum values: fast | standard | cost_efficient
  - Wire through JSON/YAML config parsing and internal runtime Config object.
- Keep existing explicit batching knobs intact (no breaking change):
  - max_batch_size
  - max_queue_delay_ms
  - prefill_weight / decode_weight (or equivalent scheduling weights)
  - kv_cache_pressure_* / admission_control_* (names vary by component)

Precedence rules (must be explicit in code + docs comments)
1) Explicit batching knobs (if set) override tier defaults for that knob.
2) batching_tier provides defaults only for knobs not explicitly set.
3) If neither explicit knobs nor batching_tier are set, preserve current behavior (today’s defaults).

Validation requirements
- Validate batching_tier value is in enum set; unknown values fail config load with clear error.
- Allow batching_tier to coexist with explicit knobs (do not hard error), but:
  - emit a structured warning log on startup: "batching_tier_set_with_overrides" including list of overridden fields
  - include guidance in error/warn text pointing users to docs (once published) and the precedence rules.
- Guardrails at schema layer (cheap sanity checks only; don’t encode perf heuristics here):
  - Reject negative values for queue delay / batch size as today.
  - If explicit max_queue_delay_ms is set and streaming is enabled (if schema can detect route type), do not change existing validation; do not add streaming-tier coupling in this ticket.

Compatibility / migration
- Backwards compatible: existing configs without batching_tier continue to work.
- No API shape changes for inference requests; this is deployment/runtime config.
- Dedicated/Private: ensure helm values and Private installer can accept and pass through batching_tier (handled in follow-on issues; but schema should not prevent that wiring).

Implementation notes
- Update config schema definitions in:
  - runtime config parsing layer (common)
  - any protobuf/JSON schema artifacts used by Console/control plane
- Add unit tests:
  - parses each enum value
  - rejects invalid string
  - precedence behavior is represented (at least in computed defaults object or in config merge logic tests)
  - warning emitted when tier + explicit overrides are present

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Runtime config schema accepts batching_tier with values fast|standard|cost_efficient.
- [x] Invalid tier values fail fast with actionable error.
- [x] Precedence rules implemented: explicit knobs override tier-provided defaults; unchanged behavior when tier unset.
- [x] Unit tests added for parsing + precedence + warning.
- [x] Change is behind feature flag only if required by config rollout policy (OK to land schema without enabling tier behavior).

Links
- Confluence PRD: workload-aware batching defaults (Cost Optimization Automation)
- Confluence design spec: workload-aware batching defaults design spec
- Related runtime logic: ENG-18421

Notes / open questions
- Naming: "cost_efficient" vs "cost-efficient". Current proposal: cost_efficient (snake case) to match existing config style.
- Whether to add alias "eco" at parse layer: not in scope unless PM insists; avoid long-term compatibility baggage.
- "effective config" endpoint is out of scope here (tracked separately; needed for Console explainers).
